title: Goose v2 Necks Build
eyebrow: Build plan for approval · Models #25, the goose v2 necks · design approved: bone spikes, S-curve, one bone per vertebra
approval: Build plan approved: goose v2 necks

short.lead: You approved vertebra ridges with a bone spike breaking out of each vertebra, a goose's S-curve, and one rig bone per vertebra. This is how I build it. It reuses the throwaway test's shapes and the version 2 build that already exists, so nothing new is added to the build itself. It takes two steps, filed as #26 and #27 under #25.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it changes.
items: Put the S-curve, ridges and spikes in the design

spec.json's version 2 neck paths take the test's S-curve. A new vertebrae block holds the counts (15 on the main neck, 12 on each side neck) and the ridge and spike sizes. goose_design.py's version 2 mode shapes the ridges and places one spike per vertebra in place of the 13 spikes on the main neck. Version 1 still gives 1,072 parts and 272,380 triangles.

items.alt: Throwaway test: S-curved necks with a bone spike per vertebra
items.caption: The look being built, from the throwaway test (untextured).

items: The full version 2 build runs with the same checks: under 300,000 triangles, 6.75 m tall within 0.15 m, and a skin of 1 piece. The test measured 2,992 extra triangles for the spikes, so, if the test's count holds, the total should be 297,820: the current goose_v2's 294,828 plus 2,992. The build refuses to export if the total goes over 300,000 triangles. Then I re-render the close-ups and views, update the docs, and change the text of #21 (the rig) to ask for 15 bones on the main neck and 12 on each side neck.
A new QA page shows the necks from the side and front, next to the version you rejected.

changes: New v2 neck paths and a vertebrae block.
S-curved paths, plus vertebra counts and sizes
Version 2 mode shapes the ridges and spikes.
Smooth tubes and 13 spikes on the main neck
Ridged tubes and one spike per vertebra on all three necks
The ridge shape is the one from the throwaway test (docs/art/reviews/goose-v2-neck-prototype/prototype_neck.py).
The fused skin and its checks work as they are.
7 bones on the main neck, 6 on each side neck
Only the issue text changes now; the rig itself is built in #21.
